baseline.harness: benches/ab.py — alternating B C C B blocks in one session on one machine; the reported delta is the median of the paired ratios, and the noise floor is the spread among repeated blocks of the SAME build. Figures before F-12 came from a single B-then-C run, which could not separate a small delta from run-order drift
baseline.instrumentation: the frozen v0.1.0-conformant wheel carries the alloc-stats counters in release; they became test-only at F-05. ab.py records baseline_instrumented/current_instrumented in ab-latest.json so a reader can see which side had them
baseline.estimator_note: Every figure recorded before the trustworthy-performance-evidence change was produced by the min-of-batches estimator: the minimum per-call time across 7 autoranged batches in one process. That estimator rewards whichever batch dodged the scheduler and has no central-limit behavior to converge on. Figures under it and under the mean-across-workers estimator that replaced it are NOT comparable, and no historical figure is restated under the new estimator without re-measurement.

roles.story: v0.1.0-conformant (.venv-baseline) — what the optimization round bought. Reported, never gated: every figure in `candidates` below is measured against it
roles.guard: v0.2.0 (.venv-guard) — the latest release, and the only thing `make ab` gates against. Re-cut it at every release or it decays into the same blind spot

candidates.hypothesis: exact-type pointer compares beat a chain of limited-API type-check calls per cell
candidates.commit: perf: E1 type-pointer dispatch + E2 row capacity reservation
candidates.note: measured together with E2; also recovered the +14-15% typed-encode regression that the wire-options plumbing introduced (caught by the A/B harness on its first run)
candidates.requalified_under_f12: the encode gain is resolved at 512 and 4096 records; at 16 and 64 it is smaller than the session noise floor and is reported as unresolved rather than as a win

candidates.hypothesis: one up-front capacity reservation for tabular rows removes growth-doubling copies
candidates.commit: perf: E1 type-pointer dispatch + E2 row capacity reservation
candidates.requalified_under_f12: the encode gain is resolved at 512 and 4096 records; at 16 and 64 it is smaller than the session noise floor and is reported as unresolved rather than as a win

candidates.hypothesis: quote-free rows (the overwhelming majority) can split on a plain memchr scan instead of byte-at-a-time quote tracking
reusing one cells buffer across rows removes an allocation per row
tabular rows repeat the same few keys; one cached PyString per column beats one fresh PyString per cell row (O(rows*cols) -> O(cols) allocations)
candidates.note: this also sped up the G3 wrapper baseline (which uses our untyped decoder), thinning typed decode's margin at 64 records to noise level in one run — resolved by implementing D1's typed-side memo rather than rejecting a genuine improvement; G3 re-verified passing at every size afterwards

candidates.hypothesis: rows of one array repeat an identical key-event sequence; record the first row's wire-name->index resolutions and replay them positionally (byte compare instead of hash per cell), with FxHash replacing SipHash for the fallback map
borrowed scalar slices need no per-cell UTF-8 revalidation after document-level validation
candidates.note: pyval.rs used unchecked conversions from the first implementation; no separate measurement possible

candidates.hypothesis: precomputed indent+delimiter templates per shape reduce writer calls per row
candidates.note: deferred: remaining encode gap vs to_builtins is getattr-bound (R-02), and E1/E2 already recovered the options regression; candidate remains open with its hypothesis intact

candidates.target: whole typed encode vs msgspec.to_builtins alone
candidates.hypothesis: E1-E3 together might close G4 at large payloads
candidates.note: G4 still fails: 2.36us vs 1.05us at 16 records, 494us vs 447us (~10% gap) at 4096. The floor remains public stable-ABI attribute reads vs msgspec's private C slot reads (canvas risk R-02). Reported, not masked.

candidates.target: strict-mode duplicate-key detection in the parser
candidates.hypothesis: note_key kept seen keys in a Vec and scanned it linearly, so an object with N keys paid O(N^2) byte comparisons; keyed tabular bodies make N the row count. An FxHashSet should turn that into O(N) and be invisible everywhere else.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard: keyed decode -18.4% at 64, -50.7% at 512, -88.0% at 4096 (MDE 0.9-1.4%); 16 and every non-keyed metric resolved no significant difference. The growth with size is the quadratic signature the hypothesis predicted.
candidates.note: The candidate arrived with its own gate-coverage warning and it was correct: the ladder had no keyed payload, so every existing metric reads flat and D6 would have been rejected as noise. benches/payloads.py gained keyed_document/keyed_toon_text and ab.py a 'keyed decode' metric BEFORE this was measured. Rejecting a real 88% win for want of a payload is the same failure as the speed gate that could not see a 24% regression.

candidates.hypothesis: classify_bare ran an integer scan and then re-scanned the same bytes through the float grammar, so every bare string paid two failed passes. One pass over the number grammar should win on every decode, and on encode too while needs_quote still calls classify_bare.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard, cumulative with D6; P2's share isolated against the D6-only run: typed decode -2.5 to -4.5%, untyped decode -3.3 to -3.5%, typed encode -6.7% at 4096. The encode win is expected at this point in the stack because needs_quote still routes through classify_bare; E5 later removes that call.
candidates.note: Verified by an exhaustive differential against the replaced two-pass implementation, kept in src/scalar.rs as a #[cfg(test)] oracle: every token up to length 5 over the alphabet that decides the grammar (0192.eE+-n) plus the edge literals, 111,126 tokens, zero divergences.

candidates.hypothesis: needs_quote made up to four passes over the same bytes (classify_bare, numeric-like, forbidden-byte, prefix checks) and write_quoted re-encoded every character through UTF-8. One pass for the decision and bulk span copies for the escaping should win on every string cell.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard, cumulative; E5's share isolated against the P2 run: typed encode -13.3 to -17.2% cumulative (E5 adds ~-10 points over P2), untyped encode -6.1 to -9.0%. Decode is unchanged by E5, as expected.
candidates.note: The pass-collapsing rests on one observation: every valid number token is also numeric-like, so the number grammar needs no separate pass in the quoting decision. Verified by differential against the replaced multi-pass implementation, kept as a #[cfg(test)] oracle: 107,841 (string, delimiter) pairs over an alphabet covering delimiters, structural bytes, controls, the number grammar and multi-byte UTF-8, plus 35,937 escape comparisons. Zero divergences. The efficiency lock independently confirms canonical bytes did not move.

candidates.target: per-cell key resolution for tabular rows (src/event.rs, parser.rs, typed.rs)
candidates.hypothesis: The D1 memo already replays the first row's key resolutions, but re-derived each key's bytes (Cow plus possible unescape) and memcmp'd per cell to verify. Rows of a tabular body all come from one header, so the parser can announce that and the typed consumer can replay purely by cursor.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard, cumulative; D5's share isolated against the E5 run: typed decode -5.9 to -8.3% cumulative, D5 adding ~3 to 4 points. Untyped decode and both encode directions unchanged, which is the expected signature since D5 touches only TypedConsumer.
candidates.note: A new `begin_tabular` consumer event carries the announcement; its default implementation is a no-op so the untyped and probe consumers are untouched. Trust is granted only when the stack top is the array's own frame (start_array fires first, verified), never inside an `Any` subtree or a skipped value, and never to a memo that declined to memoize. List-form arrays keep the untrusted verify-by-compare path. Not extended to the untyped consumer: speeding the untyped wrapper would thin G3's measured margin, which should be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect.

candidates.target: Struct field reads during encode (canvas risk R-02, gate G4)
candidates.hypothesis: Replacing N stable-ABI getattr calls per Struct instance with one msgspec.structs.astuple call — msgspec's own C slot reads through its public API — should close part of the G4 gap against msgspec.to_builtins.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard. With E7 applied, typed encode measured -5.7/-7.5/-6.6/-5.8% at 16/64/512/4096. With E7 reverted and nothing else changed, the same metric measured -20.4/-16.1/-16.6/-16.5%. E7 costs roughly 9 to 10 points of typed encode at every size. Untyped encode, which never touches a Struct, stayed flat across both runs and serves as the drift control.
candidates.note: The candidate arrived with this exact falsification condition stated — one vectorcall plus a tuple allocation per row could lose to bare getattr at narrow structs — and it fired, at every size rather than only the small ones. The challenge shape is narrow: Worker has 3 fields and Metadata 2, so write_row_obj trades 5 getattrs for 2 tuple allocations and 2 vectorcalls per row. Not adopted, and deliberately not adopted conditionally: dispatching on field count would put a magic number in the hot path and add a second field-read implementation beside the first. E7 could be revisited only with evidence from a wide-struct payload, and that payload would have to earn its place on the ladder first. G4 remains the honest miss it was; R-02 is unchanged.

candidates.target: scalar spelling on the entries path (src/encode.rs)
candidates.hypothesis: scalar_text built a String per scalar - to_string() for null/ints/text and a whole temporary Writer for quoted strings - then copied it into the writer. One allocation per key: value entry, per call. The row path never paid this, which is why an entry cost about 3x a tabular cell.
candidates.measurement: make ab vs the v0.3.0 guard on the new entry encode metric, attributed by reverting: without R2-B -2.0/-3.6/-0.7/-3.2/-5.1/-2.1% at 4/8/16/64/512/4096; with R2-B -8.2/-11.4/-18.8/-10.2/-10.1/-9.1%. R2-B's share is roughly 5 to 7 points.
candidates.note: write_scalar now writes directly using the row path's own spellings (itoa, write_float, needs_quote/write_quoted) and scalar_text is deleted, so there is one scalar-spelling implementation rather than two. Measurable only because entry_document and the entry encode metric landed first; on the old ladder every payload was tabular or keyed and this would have read as noise.

candidates.target: entry key text on the encode path (src/encode.rs)
candidates.hypothesis: object_pairs copied every key into a String per call (dict: to_str()?.to_string(); struct: field.wire.clone()) and KeyedShape copied every entry key. Borrowing the plan's text or holding the key object should remove a copy per entry per call.
candidates.measurement: entry encode vs the v0.3.0 guard: -8.2/-11.4/-18.8/-10.2/-10.1/-9.1% before, -12.0/-16.8/-13.0/-18.1/-18.2/-16.0% after, at 4/8/16/64/512/4096. R2-C adds roughly 4 to 8 points. The @16 before-reading carried a 28% MDE and is not a usable comparison point.
candidates.note: EntryText::{Wire(&str borrowed from the plan inside the Val), Object(Bound<PyString>)} reads the text at write time. Costs one to_str per dict key at write time and an incref per held key object; both measured cheaper than the copy they replace.

candidates.hypothesis: Every dict with two or more entries is probed for keyed tabular form, and the probe allocated two Vecs before looking at a single value. Most probed objects are plain configs whose first value is a scalar, which disqualifies them immediately; a first-item peek should settle that case allocation-free.
candidates.measurement: entry encode vs the v0.3.0 guard: -12.0/-16.8/-13.0/-18.1/-18.2/-16.0% before, -17.1/-18.3/-19.9/-18.9/-21.2/-22.7% after, at 4/8/16/64/512/4096. R2-D adds 2 to 7 points, largest at the small end and at 4096.
candidates.note: Full detection is unchanged; only the scalar-first miss is settled earlier. Costs one extra iter().next() on dicts that do pass detection.

candidates.target: line classification in the parser (src/scalar.rs, header.rs, parser.rs)
candidates.hypothesis: A plain `key: value` line paid up to three quote-aware scans - parse_header scanned the whole line for '[' (always a miss on this class), then for ':', then entry_colon scanned for ':' again - and `- key: value` list items paid a fourth. The first unquoted mark decides the class by itself, so one scan that stops at whichever mark comes first should replace all of them, and the dominant line class should stop at its colon instead of walking to end of line.
candidates.measurement: entry decode vs the v0.3.0 guard, attributed by reverting P3 alone. Without P3: +3.0/-5.9/-42.1/-85.2% at 16/64/512/4096. With P3: -20.5/-33.4/-57.5/-89.1%. As a ratio - the only valid framing when the effects compound - P3 is worth -23/-29/-27/-26%, essentially flat across sizes, which is what a per-line constant-cost win should look like. The container's own estimate was -24% at 512.
candidates.note: The large absolute numbers on this metric are mostly D6 from round 1, not P3: entry_document is a 4096-key root object, so the strict-mode duplicate-key set dominates it. Reading the two vs-guard deltas as a difference in points would have credited P3 with 4 points at 4096 instead of 26%. Correctness checked by a differential in src/scalar.rs: the fused scanner must report the earlier of the two marks two independent quote-aware scans find, and resolved_colon must recover the colon the fused scan skipped - 37,457 lines exhaustive to length 5 over the structural alphabet, plus quoted-key and list-item edge cases, zero divergences. The candidate's own falsification condition (tabular decode regressing from the extra branch) did not fire: untyped decode moved -3.2 to -7.3% faster and typed decode -5.7 to -9.4% faster.

token_findings.T1: PASS — canonical TOON is 0.61-0.64x compact JSON tokens (o200k_base) on the uniform-record ladder; 0.80x on string-heavy; 0.65x on numeric-heavy
token_findings.incumbents: both v3.0-era codecs cost 1.25x JSON tokens on the challenge shape — worse than the format they replace
token_findings.T2: the tab-delimiter folklore does not hold under o200k_base: differences are within a few tokens per ten thousand either way (tab wins marginally on numeric-heavy, loses one header token elsewhere); losing points published per the requirement
token_findings.T3_irregular_shapes_lose: MEASURED LOSS, published per the losing-points requirement: on irregular (non-tabular) shapes canonical TOON costs MORE tokens than compact JSON - 1.16x at 16 records, 1.19x at 512 - despite producing FEWER bytes (0.92x and 0.94x). Both numbers were already in efficiency.lock.json; the divergence had never been read. Mechanism: TOON tokenizes worse per byte than JSON (2.26 vs 2.83 bytes/token on this payload) because JSON's punctuation is saturated in the o200k_base merge table while TOON's indentation and `key: value` runs are not. So the token win is not the byte win: TOON needs roughly a 0.77x byte ratio just to break even on tokens. Tabular clears it (0.37x bytes -> 0.61x tokens); entry-by-entry does not (0.94x bytes -> 1.19x tokens). The token advantage is a property of the tabular forms specifically, not of TOON.
token_findings.T4_indent_axis_unmeasured: CLOSED by round 2: the indent axis is now in benches/bench_tokens.py (INDENT_AXIS = 1,2,4) with decode-roundtrip assertions, and the matrix is generated rather than asserted. indent=1 saves tokens on EVERY shape, not only the entry-heavy ones: ~4 points on the tabular ladder (uniform@4096 0.621 -> 0.579 vs JSON, 60,455 -> 56,359 tokens) because a single leading space merges into the first cell's token where two spaces cost their own token per row, and 13-15 points on irregular. indent=4 costs bytes and is token-identical to indent=2 (space runs merge), so there is no token reason to use it. Canonical stays indent=2 and the lock never moves; this is a caller's option. Reproduced independently before adoption.
token_findings.T5_tabular_fallback_rulings: The three shapes where the encoder falls back from tabular were checked against TOON 4.1.1 at the pinned corpus commit 62f16b3, section 9.3: a row missing a key, an Optional[Struct] that is None in one row, and an array-valued column. All three fallbacks are REQUIRED by the spec, and detection is MUST in both directions, so the classifier can be neither more nor less aggressive than it is. No code change recovers tokens on these shapes. Corroboration strength differs and is recorded honestly: the first two are confirmed by encode fixtures in the vendored corpus whose names state the rule outright ('uses list form for objects with different fields'; 'falls back to list form when a column mixes ...'), while the array-valued-column ruling has ZERO fixture coverage and rests on the spec reading alone. The remaining token levers are payload shape (caller-side) and the indent option.

instrumentation_cost.question: what did the release-wheel G2 counters cost the sides that carried them?
instrumentation_cost.method: benches/ab.py --baseline-venv .venv-g2 — instrumented vs clean, same commit, same session
instrumentation_cost.result: not resolvable by this harness: every row placed the CLEAN build 0.4-3.6% slower, which cannot be a real effect of removing work
instrumentation_cost.conclusion: the counters were a proof-quality defect, not a measurable speed defect; the published G3/G5 margins were not materially inflated by them
instrumentation_cost.follow_on: the sign-consistent penalty on the second-run side independently reproduces F-12: baseline always runs first, and run order is worth 1-3% — larger than the effect under test

run_order_drift.question: how much of a published delta is the machine rather than the code?
run_order_drift.method: benches/ab.py --rounds 2 — eight blocks, B C C B twice; noise floor is the spread among the four blocks of each build
run_order_drift.result: same-build blocks disagree by 1.7-8.8 percentage points depending on metric and size; an earlier single-order run put whichever side ran second 0.4-3.6% slower on every row
run_order_drift.consequence: decode deltas (-13 to -20%) sit well above the floor and are resolved; typed-encode at 16 and 64 records (-5.4%, -4.2%) sits BELOW it and is not a result on this machine
run_order_drift.action: ab.py now labels below-noise rows explicitly and keeps every block in benches/ab-latest.json

worker_count_choice.question: how many worker processes does the mean-across-workers estimator need?
worker_count_choice.method: bench_typed at 16 records with 8 workers; read the per-worker coefficient of variation, then compute the standard error of the published mean as CV/sqrt(workers)
worker_count_choice.result: per-worker CV on a quiet machine: typed decode 0.80%, typed encode 1.43%, to_builtins 1.13%, wrapper decode 1.18%. Standard error at 10 workers: 0.25-0.45%
worker_count_choice.choice: 10 workers. The smallest count whose standard error sits well under the >=4% effects this project reports; 25 workers would buy about 0.15 percentage points for 2.5x the runtime
worker_count_choice.caveat: per-worker CV is a property of machine load, not of the codec: the same metric measured 7.84% CV during a heavily loaded moment in the same session. The standard error above is a quiet-machine figure

ab_false_positive_check.question: does the significance gate stay quiet when nothing changed?
ab_false_positive_check.method: benches/ab.py --baseline-venv .venv — the current build against itself, 8 metrics
ab_false_positive_check.result: first pass: 7 of 8 quiet, and typed encode@512 reported +1.6% SLOWER with a 1.4% minimum detectable effect — a false positive, as expected from 8 tests at alpha 0.95
ab_false_positive_check.consequence: a slowdown now triggers an independent confirmation run and only a reproduced slowdown fails the gate; re-run returned 8 of 8 no-significant-difference and exit 0

gate_reference_point.question: can the speed gate detect a regression at all?
gate_reference_point.method: inject a heap allocation per placed value into the typed decode path (139 -> 172 us, a 24% slowdown), then run the gate
gate_reference_point.result: against the STORY baseline the same 24% regression read as +2.2%, verdict 'no significant difference', exit 0 — the current build led that baseline by 15-20%, so the regression only erased the lead. Against the GUARD baseline it read +24.4%, reproduced on the confirmation run, exit 1
gate_reference_point.consequence: the gate measures against the latest release; the frozen tag stays as the reported story. A first attempt at a slowdown (black_box over 40 additions) compiled away to 137.67 us vs 139.03 clean, and the gate correctly stayed quiet

open_question_encode_4096.question: is there a small typed-encode regression at 4096 records against v0.2.0?
open_question_encode_4096.status: RESOLVED — yes, and it is real
open_question_encode_4096.evidence: 16 blocks per side, one metric per block, guard CV 1.08% and current CV 3.64%: +2.42% with a 1.98% minimum detectable effect, significant. Earlier runs that could not resolve it were underpowered (2-3 rounds) or contended (one had 40.8% CV on the current side, and the t-test correctly refused to call a +29.8% reading)
open_question_encode_4096.attribution: reverting ONLY the two encode-path changes since v0.2.0 (the build_shape depth guard and the capped writer reservation) moved it to +1.38%, still significant. Both run about five times per encode of 4096 records, so neither can plausibly cost 1% of a 500us call; the residual and probably the whole effect is binary layout and inlining changed by the new modules, which is a known measurement phenomenon rather than a code defect
open_question_encode_4096.next: belongs to the profiling work (Phase E), not to a revert: the logic is O(1) per array and the corpus, containment tests, and G2 all depend on it

confirmation_power.question: is a same-power confirmation run enough to reject a false positive?
confirmation_power.result: no. typed encode@4096 flagged at +2.5% and its same-power confirmation reproduced it; a 3-round run then read +2.1% with a 2.6% MDE, i.e. not significant
confirmation_power.consequence: confirmation now runs at double the block count, so it has more power than the test that raised the flag rather than the same

ab_block_cost.question: why did a gate run take ten minutes?
ab_block_cost.cause: each A/B block called a sampler that measured every metric in the module and reported one, so every typed-encode block also timed the python-toon incumbent at ~30ms a call
ab_block_cost.fix: MSGSPEC_TOON_ONLY_METRIC makes the sampler skip metrics the block will discard; a 4096 typed-encode block fell from about 4s to 0.5s
ab_block_cost.caveat: the sampler metric name is now listed in the METRICS table rather than derived from the result key — deriving it silently mismatched half the metrics, and a block that measures nothing reports a mean of zero

ab_python_profile_H5.question: how much of an A/B block is Python harness work outside the three published samples?
ab_python_profile_H5.method: cProfile around 8 parent run_block calls plus a child profile of bench_typed.sample_run for entry decode@512 with the guard's fixed 1024-loop count
ab_python_profile_H5.result: mean block wall 0.4369s; the three published samples account for 0.2971s; 0.1398s (32%) is non-published work. About 0.097s is the deliberate discarded warmup. Parent Python is negligible: cProfile attributes 3.484 of 3.495s to subprocess polling. Child imports cost about 0.035s and sample_run performs about 0.028s of setup outside measure, including unrelated python-toon encode/decode validation.
ab_python_profile_H5.ruling: ADOPTED. process isolation, imports, and one discarded sample stay because the estimator intentionally measures between-process variance and warms each process. Metric-unrelated payload and incumbent setup was removed. Child setup outside measure fell from about 0.028s to 0.002s; a 20-pair alternating fixed-one-loop diagnostic fell from 43.04ms to 34.24ms per process (-20.5%). Full sampler paths retain every setup/assertion. A source-identical 8-block-per-side comparison remained parity (+0.3%, no significant difference; noisy 6.7% MDE). The current-side calibration block also stays: it cannot warm a later interpreter, but it does symmetrically fault in that build's binary/code pages before measured sweeps.

functional_surface_P4a.question: does constructing Encoder/Decoder inside each package-level encode/decode call create a resolvable fixed cost?
functional_surface_P4a.method: add functional encode/decode rows to the existing mean-across-10-workers typed ladder; reusable and functional calls run in the same worker session
functional_surface_P4a.result: at 16 records functional decode was 8.89us versus 4.77us reusable (+86%), and functional encode was 4.97us versus 2.01us reusable (+147%). Premiums fell to +27%/+42% at 64 and +5%/+10% at 512; the 4096 differences were noise-shaped (+0.6%/-2.1%).
functional_surface_P4a.ruling: CONFIRMED. Attempt one bounded reuse design for the functional surface. Reject any cache that can retain arbitrary user classes without a stated bound.

functional_decode_native_plan_P4b.question: can functional typed decode reuse compiled metadata without caching codec wrapper objects?
functional_decode_native_plan_P4b.method: port msgspec 0.21.1's compiled Struct metadata pattern: cache an opaque native CompiledPlan behind the existing 512-entry annotation LRU, then clone its Arc into each Decoder; compare functional decode to the v0.4.0 guard for three B-C-C-B rounds
functional_decode_native_plan_P4b.result: typed Decoder construction fell from about 3.36us to 0.21us. Functional decode moved -40.0% at 16 records, -15.7% at 64, and -4.5% at 512; -3.0% at 4096 was below the run's 3.2% MDE.
functional_decode_native_plan_P4b.ruling: ADOPTED. No Decoder object is cached. The same bounded annotation cache owns both the public PlanSpec and opaque native compiled plan; each decode still uses local consumer/parser state. Two full ladders flagged different unreachable encode rows; neither repeated across full runs or survived a longer focused control, exposing the 54-row gate's family-wise false-positive problem (H6), not a stable candidate regression.

encode_first_byte_quote_split_E8.question: can strings with a nonnumeric first byte skip numeric-state tracking in needs_quote without changing canonical bytes?
encode_first_byte_quote_split_E8.method: port serde_toon_format's first-byte analysis split while retaining a full wire-syntax scan; validate against the existing 107841-case differential oracle and compare the affected encode surfaces to the v0.4.0 guard for three B-C-C-B rounds
encode_first_byte_quote_split_E8.result: zero differential divergences. Across 16/64/512/4096 records: typed encode -3.0/-4.4/-5.3/-4.2%, entry encode -16.5/-16.7/-17.1/-17.1%, untyped encode -2.7/-3.1/-4.0/-3.2%. Functional encode was no significant difference at 16 (-1.3%, MDE 1.8%) and faster at 64/512/4096 (-2.4/-4.6/-4.7%).
encode_first_byte_quote_split_E8.ruling: ADOPTED. This is a bounded native specialization derived from prior art, not a grammar change. Corpus 538/538, 36 Rust tests, 119 Python tests, payload safety, and G2 remained green.

functional_encode_native_plan_P4c.question: can functional Struct encode reuse immutable native field and static-shape metadata behind the existing bounded class cache?
functional_encode_native_plan_P4c.method: cache an opaque Arc<EncodePlan> in the existing 512-entry Python LRU, retain local Encoder writer/hook/runtime state, and compare with an immutable checkpoint-15 wheel for three B-C-C-B rounds
functional_encode_native_plan_P4c.result: functional encode moved -1.8/-2.1/+0.3/+0.0% at 16/64/512/4096 records; no row was significant (MDE 5.1/2.2/1.6/1.6%).
functional_encode_native_plan_P4c.ruling: REJECTED and reverted. Python already cached PlanSpec lowering, and the remaining native field/shape compilation does not materially move whole-call cost. Do not retry without a new measured mechanism.

combined_quote_delimiter_scan_D7.question: does one memchr2 quote/delimiter scan beat the existing quote-presence pass followed by delimiter iteration on common quote-free rows?
combined_quote_delimiter_scan_D7.method: preserve the old splitter as a 411771-row differential oracle, then run three-round focused A/B on typed, entry, and untyped decode at 16/64/512/4096 records
combined_quote_delimiter_scan_D7.result: zero semantic divergences, but no significant decode win. Entry stayed within -0.6% to +0.3%; typed had no reproduced change; untyped trended slower at +7.0/+2.5/+2.6/+0.8%, below the per-row MDEs.
combined_quote_delimiter_scan_D7.ruling: REJECTED and reverted. The stated typed/untyped-win falsifier fired. The existing two-pass quote-free path remains.

cold_any_forwarding_D8.question: does guarding before AnyEvent construction and outlining forwarding remove measurable cost when no Any subtree is active?
cold_any_forwarding_D8.method: leave the existing Any/untyped sub-consumer state machine intact, add six hot-path presence guards, mark forwarding cold and noinline, then run three-round focused typed-decode A/B
cold_any_forwarding_D8.result: typed decode improved -9.0/-10.0/-9.3/-7.1% at 16/64/512/4096 records with 0.8-1.3% MDEs.

wide_dictionary_diagnostic_E9.question: does a permanent 64-column dict-row payload expose the shape-classifier cost before changing membership?

wide_dictionary_diagnostic_E9.result: 22.72/44.38/88.30/355.39/2944.27us, or 5.52-5.75us per row. Source contains nested per-row-key linear scans of first_keys. toon-rust 2136cb1 independently uses IndexMap::contains_key for the equivalent v3 check.
wide_dictionary_diagnostic_E9.ruling: DIAGNOSTIC ADOPTED. Attempt hashed first-row membership next; retain only if the wide row wins without regressing the canonical five-column ladders.

hashed_dictionary_membership_E9.question: can equal-length later rows prove TOON 4.1 key-set equality by hashing the first row's key objects instead of linearly scanning copied strings?
hashed_dictionary_membership_E9.method: reuse first-row Python key objects, check every one with PyDict_Contains in each later row, lock varying-order and same-width-different-set behavior, then compare with the immutable checkpoint-19 wheel
hashed_dictionary_membership_E9.result: wide dict encode improved -58.1/-61.9/-66.9/-67.9/-67.4% at 4/8/16/64/512 rows. Untyped encode improved -31.5/-37.2/-37.1/-36.9% at 16/64/512/4096. Typed Struct encode was parity-to-faster.
hashed_dictionary_membership_E9.ruling: ADOPTED. The official TOON 4.1 spec requires the same key set while permitting per-row order variation; equal lengths plus membership of every first-row key is equivalent. Corpus 538/538, 36 Rust tests, 121 Python tests, payload safety, and G2 remained green.

harness_findings.H1_loop_counts_were_calibrated_per_side: The A/B gate could not certify parity: with the guard re-cut from the SAME commit as the working tree, make ab reported reproduced slowdowns on 2 of 42 metrics, twice running, with four of six flags landing at records=64. Cause: ab.py spawned a fresh process per block and _timing calibrated a loop count independently in each one, while _timing already exposed LOOPS_ENV for exactly this and ab.py never used it. _calibrate doubles from 1, so two builds a few percent apart near a boundary land on counts differing by 2x and the two sides stop measuring the same amount of work. A freshly cut guard is additionally cold on its first run and that run chose its loop count: a guard built moments earlier calibrated to 256 loops at 323us where every later run agreed on 512 loops at 127us. Fixed by calibrate_metric: one discarded block per side warms both interpreters and fixes the loop count both then measure with. Effect on the parity run: typed decode@64 +7.2% SLOWER -> +0.2% no significant difference; keyed decode@64 +4.5% SLOWER -> +0.6% no significant difference.
harness_findings.H2_residual_drift_across_a_long_run: LARGELY FIXED by deterministic interleaving (external review round 3, patch 01 of 1). Originally: After H1, a residual false positive remains: entry decode@4096 read +1.6% and +2.2% (reproduced at double blocks) inside full 42-metric runs, but +0.1/+0.6/+0.2% when that metric is run alone. The bias is therefore run-order drift accumulating across a ~6 minute continuous ladder, not a difference between the two builds. The ABBA block design controls drift WITHIN one metric's blocks; nothing controls drift ACROSS metrics, and the per-metric minimum detectable effect cannot see it. Consequence: make ab currently cannot certify parity below roughly 2% on a full run, which is well above the sub-1% MDE it prints. Candidate fixes: round-robin the metric order instead of finishing each metric before starting the next, randomize metric order per run, or re-measure a canary metric at the start and end and report the drift alongside every verdict. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, which is the same failure mode as a gate that cannot fire. || RESOLUTION: every block-position of the B C C B pattern now runs across ALL metric points before the next position runs anywhere, so each metric's baseline and current samples both span the full run and slow drift enters both sides symmetrically - bias becomes variance, which the t-test models and the MDE reports. No threshold, alpha or block count changed; the ABBA property survives because a metric still sees B at sweep 1, C at 2, C at 3, B at 4. A canary metric is read at start/mid/end and reported beside every run, never gating. Confirmation runs the flagged metric alone after the ladder. Measured on identical source: old harness 2 reproduced slowdowns in each of two runs (up to +7.2%); new harness 1 reproduced then 0, with peak false-positive magnitude down from +7.2% to +1.8%. Options 2 (randomised order) and 4 (empirical floor) were rejected by the author on this project's own grounds - nondeterminism in evidence, and a floor being structurally the 'bigger threshold' the acceptance text bans.
harness_findings.H3_build_identity_floor: CLOSED, with the proposed mechanism falsified. v0.4.0 source was built from a third path (/private/tmp/msgspec-toon-h3-src), installed as a wheel in .venv-h3, and compared against the v0.4.0 guard with 8 blocks per side on the previously biased entry decode@512 point. Result: -0.5%, MDE 1.1%, no significant difference; canary spread 2.5%. A third source path did NOT reproduce the old +1.0 to +1.8% sign, so source-path-driven binary layout is not confirmed and must not be stated as the permanent cause. Published resolution: a focused same-source comparison resolved only changes larger than 1.1% in this session; the full-ladder practical floor remains roughly 1-2% on quiet rows and higher where the per-row MDE says so. ab.py gained --current-venv so this comparison names both immutable wheel environments instead of swapping the editable working extension.
harness_findings.H4_solo_confirmation_can_false_negative: OPEN. The gate was proven to FIRE, which the round-3 submission did not test - its acceptance evidence was entirely 'zero false positives on identical source', a property any broken gate has. A deliberate perturbation (one 96-byte allocation per scanned line in scan_line_marks) produced a real 10-20% regression: entry decode reproduced SLOWER at 4, 8, 16, 64 and 512, and the run failed. But entry decode@4096 flagged at +10.0% (MDE 1.7%) in the ladder and then did NOT reproduce in the solo confirmation - a false negative on a genuine 10% regression at the largest, noisiest block. The gate still failed the run overall, so this is a weakness rather than a defect, but a confirmation step that can miss 10% is not a confirmation step to rely on alone.
